procs.rm: Liquid and solid feedstocks, solvents, catalysts, additives
procs.ut: Power (pumps, agitators), nitrogen blanketing, steam tracing
procs.out: Released, inventoried raw materials at the plant battery limit
procs.q: Purity %, moisture, impurity profile, density, certificate-of-analysis match

uc.t: Incoming Material Quality & Supplier Variability Analytics
d: Analyses certificates of analysis, incoming QC results and downstream batch outcomes for every lot and supplier.
Detects lots and suppliers whose impurity profile drifts, and links raw material variation to yield and quality losses downstream.
Provides lot-level release advisories, blending suggestions and supplier scorecards for procurement.
p: Raw material variation shows up later as batch failures or off-spec product
Certificate-of-analysis values are rarely checked against plant outcomes
QC release decisions depend on a few lab results and experience
Supplier performance is discussed on anecdote rather than data
kpi: Batch failures traced to raw material

uc.t: Tank Farm Inventory, Transfer & Loss Monitoring
d: Analyses tank levels, temperatures, densities, transfer flows and receipt and dispatch records across the tank farm.
Detects unaccounted losses, mismatched transfers, wrong-tank routing and abnormal level changes.
Provides live mass balance by tank, transfer reconciliation and alerts for overfill and contamination risk.
p: Book stock and measured stock rarely match
Transfer errors and wrong-line routing cause cross-contamination
Overfill and loss-of-containment risk on manual transfers
Month-end reconciliation is slow and manual

procs.rm: Charged raw materials, intermediates, catalysts, solvents
procs.ut: Steam, thermic fluid, cooling water, chilled brine, nitrogen, power (agitators)
procs.out: Reaction mass to work-up and purification
procs.q: Conversion %, selectivity, impurity profile, end-point parameters, batch cycle time

uc.t: Golden Batch Profiling & Batch Deviation Detection
d: Analyses temperature, pressure, dosing, agitation and jacket profiles of every past batch alongside its lab results.
Builds the golden batch envelope for each product and detects live batches drifting away from it phase by phase.
Provides early deviation alerts and corrective advisories while the batch can still be saved.
p: Batch-to-batch variation in yield and quality with no clear cause
Deviations are found only when lab results come back
Best-operator know-how is not captured in the recipe
Rework and reprocessing consume reactor time

uc.t: Reaction End-Point Prediction & Cycle Time Optimisation
d: Analyses heat-flow, dosing, pressure and inline analyser data together with in-process lab samples.
Predicts conversion and reaction end-point in real time with a soft sensor, between lab samples.
Provides end-point advisories so batches are neither stopped early nor held longer than needed.
p: Batches held 'to be safe' while waiting for lab confirmation
In-process sampling is slow and exposes operators
Cycle time varies widely between shifts
Reactor capacity is the bottleneck for the plant

d: Analyses reactor temperature, jacket duty, dosing rate, pressure and agitator power during exothermic steps.
Detects heat accumulation, cooling shortfall and dosing-to-cooling mismatch before the safety interlocks trip.
Provides graded alerts and dosing hold advisories to operators, alongside (never replacing) the safety system.
p: Exothermic steps depend on manual dosing control
Cooling capacity margins are not visible live
Near-misses are investigated only after the event
Conservative dosing slows the batch to stay safe

procs.q: Conversion %, selectivity, by-product formation, catalyst activity

d: Analyses feed composition, temperature profile, pressure, residence time and analyser data across operating history.
Models how conversion and selectivity respond to each operating condition, including recycle effects.
Provides setpoint advisories that keep the reactor at the most profitable operating point within its limits.
p: Reactors run at conservative, habit-based setpoints
By-product formation rises without anyone noticing
Feed changes are not followed by setpoint changes
Lab analysis is too slow to steer the reactor

d: Analyses temperature profiles, pressure drop, conversion and selectivity over the catalyst life.
Tracks deactivation, predicts end of run and compares catalyst batches and suppliers.
Provides changeout planning insights and operating advisories that extend useful catalyst life.
p: Catalyst changeouts scheduled by calendar, not condition
Unexpected activity loss forces unplanned shutdowns
Catalyst performance is hard to compare between charges
Operating to compensate for deactivation raises energy use

procs.rm: Reaction mass, crude product, spent solvent
procs.ut: Steam (reboilers), cooling water, chilled water, vacuum, power
procs.q: Product purity %, solvent recovery %, residue content

d: Analyses column temperatures, pressure, reflux, reboiler steam and product analysers.
Builds soft sensors for top and bottom purity and finds where the column is over-purifying.
Provides reflux and steam advisories that hold purity on target at the lowest energy use.
p: Columns over-purify to avoid off-spec product
Steam per tonne varies widely between shifts
Purity is known only from periodic lab samples
Flooding and weeping episodes cut capacity

d: Analyses solvent purchases, recovery column performance, tank inventories and vent and effluent data.
Detects where solvent is being lost: vents, residues, effluent or poor recovery.
Provides a live solvent balance by area with loss alerts and recovery improvement advisories.
p: Solvent make-up is a large, poorly explained cost
Losses are found only at month-end
Vent and effluent losses also create compliance exposure
Recovered solvent quality varies
kpi: Solvent make-up per tonne of product

procs.ut: Steam or hot water, chilled brine, nitrogen, vacuum, power
procs.q: Particle size distribution, moisture / loss on drying, purity, colour, bulk density

d: Analyses cooling profiles, seeding, agitation, filtration time and particle size results by batch.
Links crystalliser conditions to particle size, filtration time and cake wash quality.
Provides cooling and seeding advisories that give consistent crystals and faster filtration.
p: Fine crystals clog filters and stretch filtration time
Particle size varies from batch to batch
Wash effectiveness is not measured, so impurities carry over
Centrifuges and filters become the bottleneck

d: Analyses product temperature, exhaust humidity and temperature, vacuum and heating media data.
Predicts moisture content during drying and detects the true end-point.
Provides end-point and heating advisories that stop over-drying, save energy and protect heat-sensitive products.
p: Dryers run on fixed times with safety margins
Over-drying degrades product and wastes energy
Moisture known only from offline samples
Dryer cycle limits plant output

procs.out: Packed, labelled product ready for dispatch
procs.q: Fill weight accuracy, label and batch code correctness, seal and container integrity

uc.t: Packing Line Fill Weight, Label & Seal Inspection
loc: Label applicators and batch code printers
d: Analyses camera feeds and checkweigher data on every container leaving the packing line.
Detects wrong or missing labels, unreadable batch codes, damaged containers, open seals and over-filling.
Provides automatic reject signals, line-level alerts and a traceable record for every pack.
p: Mislabelled or mis-coded packs reach customers
Over-filling gives product away on every container
Manual checks cover only a sample of packs
Customer complaints are hard to trace back to a line and shift

d: Links raw material lots, batches, equipment, operators, QC results and packs into one genealogy record.
Traces any customer complaint or deviation back through every batch and lot it touched, and forward to every affected shipment.
Provides one-click traceability reports for audits, recalls and customer queries.
p: Traceability depends on paper batch records and spreadsheets
Complaint investigations take days
Scope of a recall is unclear without full genealogy
Customer and regulatory audits are labour-intensive

d: Analyses fuel, air, flue gas, feedwater and steam flows across boilers and the plant steam headers.
Calculates live boiler efficiency and finds excess air, blowdown losses, letdown losses and steam trap failures.
Provides load sharing, combustion and header pressure advisories across the steam network.
p: Boiler efficiency is checked only during audits
Steam demand swings with batch schedules
Pressure-reducing letdowns waste available energy
Steam losses across the plant are not visible

d: Analyses chiller loads, brine and cooling water temperatures, compressor power and ambient conditions.
Calculates live efficiency per chiller and cooling tower and detects fouling, low charge and poor sequencing.
Provides sequencing and setpoint advisories that meet process cooling demand at the lowest power.
p: Chillers run in fixed combinations regardless of load
Brine temperature set lower than reactors need
Condenser fouling raises power use without warning
Cooling shortfalls slow exothermic steps

uc.t: Compressed Air, Nitrogen & Vacuum System Optimisation
d: Analyses compressor, nitrogen generator and vacuum pump loads, pressures, flows and consumption by area.
Detects leaks, artificial demand from high header pressure and inefficient machine sequencing.
Provides pressure setpoint, sequencing and leak-repair advisories with the savings tracked.
p: Air and nitrogen leaks run unchecked
Header pressure set high for the most demanding user
Nitrogen used for inerting is not measured by area
Vacuum systems run whether or not they are needed
kpi: Specific power per unit of air
Nitrogen use per tonne of product

procs.out: Treated water for reuse or discharge, sludge, salts
procs.q: COD, BOD, TDS, pH, specific pollutants, stack and vent emissions

d: Analyses inflow load, pH, COD, dissolved oxygen, sludge and dosing data through every treatment stage.
Predicts treated water quality ahead of lab results and links load spikes back to their source plant.
Provides dosing and aeration advisories and early warnings of breaches against consent limits.
p: Shock loads from batch discharges upset biological treatment
Chemicals and aeration dosed by habit
Breaches are found after the fact from lab results
Evaporators and ZLD systems are energy-hungry
kpi: Aeration power per kg COD removed

d: Analyses continuous emission monitors, scrubber performance, vent flows and leak detection survey data.
Detects emission trends approaching limits, scrubber underperformance and repeat leak points.
Provides compliance dashboards, early breach alerts and regulator-ready reports.
p: Emission excursions noticed only after they happen
Scrubber performance is not tracked against the load it treats
Leak detection and repair runs on paper
Regulatory reporting is manual and slow

d: Analyses fixed gas detectors, flame detectors, area cameras and wind data across the plant.
Detects slow-building leaks, detector faults and patterns of repeat releases at the same equipment.
Provides early leak alerts with location, likely source and affected zone, plus detector health reports.
p: Small leaks build up before reaching alarm levels
Faulty or drifting detectors go unnoticed
Alarm floods during incidents hide the real source
Repeat leak points are not tracked

uc.t: PPE, Restricted Zone & Unsafe Act Detection
loc: Tank farm and tanker unloading bays
d: Analyses existing CCTV feeds with person detection at high-risk work areas.
Detects missing helmets, goggles, chemical suits or respirators, entry into restricted zones and unsafe acts during charging.
Provides real-time alerts to supervisors, zone-wise dashboards and audit-ready evidence logs.
p: PPE checks rely on supervisor rounds
Chemical exposure risk during charging and unloading
Restricted areas entered without permits
Safety audits lack evidence

d: Analyses DCS alarm and event logs, operator actions and shift records.
Finds chattering, standing and duplicate alarms and periods when operators are overloaded.
Provides a prioritised alarm clean-up list and live operator load indicators.
p: Too many alarms for operators to act on
Nuisance alarms train operators to ignore warnings
Alarm floods during upsets
No measure of how loaded each console is

d: Analyses vibration, temperature, current and process data on pumps, agitators, compressors, centrifuges, blowers and fans.
Detects bearing faults, imbalance, misalignment, cavitation and seal problems early.
Provides fault diagnoses with recommended actions and remaining-life insights for maintenance planning.
p: Agitator and pump failures stop batches mid-way
Seal failures cause leaks and exposure
Maintenance is calendar-based or reactive
Critical spares are not planned against condition

d: Analyses flows and temperatures across condensers, reboilers, jackets and process exchangers.
Tracks heat transfer performance and predicts when fouling will start to limit the process.
Provides cleaning schedules that balance cleaning cost against lost throughput and energy.
p: Fouling slowly reduces cooling and heating capacity
Exchangers cleaned too early or too late
Fouled jackets stretch batch cycle times
Energy losses from fouling are not measured

d: Analyses corrosion probes, thickness surveys, process chemistry and operating conditions for vessels, piping and tanks.
Links corrosion rates to process conditions such as temperature, pH and chloride, and flags assets nearing limits.
Provides risk-based inspection priorities and operating window alerts.
p: Corrosive services cause unplanned leaks
Inspection data sits in reports, not linked to process data
Operating outside safe windows is noticed late
Inspection effort is spread evenly instead of by risk

uc.t: Specific Energy & Carbon Intensity Tracking by Product
d: Analyses power, steam, fuel and utility consumption by plant, product and batch.
Calculates energy and carbon per tonne of each product and benchmarks batches and shifts against their best.
Provides deviation alerts, product carbon footprints and reports for customers and ESG disclosures.
p: Energy use is known for the site, not for each product
Customers increasingly ask for product carbon footprints
No baseline to prove energy projects worked
ESG reporting is assembled by hand

d: Combines LIMS results with process data for every batch and stage.
Predicts final quality from in-process data and flags batches likely to fail before they reach QC.
Provides early quality warnings and supports faster, evidence-based release.
p: Quality failures found only at final testing
Release waits on long lab queues
Process and lab data live in separate systems
Root cause of quality issues takes days to find

d: Analyses orders, recipes, equipment availability, cleaning requirements and changeover history.
Sequences products to cut changeovers and cleaning, and spots equipment becoming the bottleneck.
Provides schedule recommendations and live adherence tracking for planners and shift leads.
p: Frequent changeovers on multi-product equipment
Cleaning time between products limits output
Schedules built in spreadsheets and changed daily
Bottlenecks shift with the product mix

uc.vt: Enabler for all other use cases
d: Connects DCS, PLC, batch systems, historians, LIMS, ERP, energy meters and cameras through I/O Connect.
Organises the data by plant, unit, equipment, batch and product so every use case reads from one model.
Provides the secure data layer, dashboards and alerting that every other use case on this page runs on.
p: Data spread across DCS, batch, lab and ERP systems
Each analytics project starts with fresh data plumbing
Batch context missing from historian data
Plant network security concerns slow integration
kpi: Use cases live on the platform
Time to deploy a new use case
